core_obligations: Dispose of the case n = 0, where every sheaf is m-regular for all m (proof lines 6666-6667).
Replace k by an infinite overfield via the base-field invariance of m-regularity, so that the section's induction step applies (proof lines 6668-6670).
Apply the restriction lemma to see that G is m-regular, and the induction on n to see that G is (m+1)-regular (proof lines 6671-6673).

Use the long exact cohomology sequence of 0 -> F(m-i) -> F(m+1-i) -> i_*G(m+1-i) -> 0 to deduce the vanishing of H^i(P^n, F(m+1-i)) for i >= 1 from the known vanishings of the corresponding groups for F(m-i) and G(m+1-i) (proof lines 6673-6683).
proof_roadmap: Induct on n with the trivial base case.
Enlarge the base field so the induction step applies.
Transfer m-regularity to the restriction to a hyperplane.
Compare the shifted sequences and deduce the extra vanishing.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that an m-regular coherent sheaf on projective n-space is also (m+1)-regular. The proof inducts on n and first replaces k by an infinite overfield using the base-field invariance of m-regularity, so that the induction step of the section may be applied (proof lines 6666-6670). Then G is m-regular by the restriction lemma and (m+1)-regular by induction, and the long exact cohomology sequence of 0 -> F(m-i) -> F(m+1-i) -> i_*G(m+1-i) -> 0 lets one deduce the vanishing of H^i(P^n, F(m+1-i)) for i >= 1 from the known vanishings for F(m-i) and G(m+1-i) (proof lines 6671-6683). H2: the induction on n combined with the long exact sequence comparison across the two shifts is the substance.
